title: Triple-SDK credential fallback and streaming ergonomics: unify interfaces, parity fixes, and version sync
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Python/TS/Go SDKs: introduce credential fallback chain, normalize streaming iterables, ergonomic retry presets, and bump SDK versions (py 1.12.0, ts 2.8.0, go 0.9.7).
description: Context: Customers and SDK consumers reported inconsistent behavior when token providers returned transient failures during long-lived streaming sessions and small discrepancies in ergonomic defaults across languages. This PR harmonizes the credential fallback semantics across Python/TypeScript/Go SDKs, unifies streaming consumer ergonomics (cancel/heartbeat/reconnect hooks), introduces named retry presets aligned with Redwood's runtime, and bumps SDK versions. Motivation: reduce customer confusion, remove subtle footguns in long-lived streams, and make cross-language migrations simpler. Changes in this PR: - Add CredentialFallbackChain abstraction (implementation per-language but matching public surface) so SDKs will try (in order): cached token -> delegated refresh provider -> platform credential adapter -> transparent reauth hook. - Normalize TTL/heartbeat defaults for streaming sessions to 10s heartbeat / 60s refresh window with explicit opt-out. - Introduce retry presets: conservative|balanced|aggressive which map to timeouts, backoff multipliers and idempotency predicates. - Surface lightweight stream handle with .cancel(), .pause_backoff(), .resume() across SDKs and document behavior in examples. - Add migration notes and a small compatibility shim for older token providers that returned plain strings. Checklist: [x] implement credential chain in all SDKs, [x] tests for credential fallback and streaming reconnect, [x] sparse e2e in canary infra (perf-canary), [x] docs and migration guide, [x] version bumps and changelogs. Reference work items: ENG-2109, ENG-2113, SUP-3421. Rollout plan: merge to main, publish SDK pre-releases for a week, monitor canary customers (billing tags: sdk-beta), then GA. Considerations: avoided changing auth wire protocol; this is strictly SDK surface and consumer behavior. Backwards compatibility shim included for the most common legacy pattern.

review_comments: Marco Ruiz: Left a couple of inline notes on typescript streamHandle; please clarify lifecycle semantics for .pause_backoff().
Aisha Patel: Responded - .pause_backoff() pauses retry backoff timers but keeps heartbeat alive; added comments and unit test to show expected ordering.
Ling Chen: Noted that Go fallback.go uses a goroutine-per-request for refresh; suggested switching to shared refresh scheduler to reduce goroutine churn.
Aisha Patel: Updated go implementation to use a shared scheduler and added benchmark showing <2% overhead on heavy stream load.
Samir Gupta: Asked for a short migration snippet for legacy token providers returning plain strings; requested docs example.
Aisha Patel: Added migration snippet and compatibility shim in all three SDKs; tests added to cover shim behavior.
ci_summary: CI: unit (py/ts/go) ✅, integration-canary ⏳ (flaky stream-test rerun passed), lint/format ✅, docs build ✅. One intermittent TS stream test failed on first run (timeout) -> re-run passed. All final checks green.
manual_testing: Locally exercised long-running stream with simulated token rotation; ran perf-canary with 50 parallel streams for 30 minutes, observed stable reconnects and expected heartbeat traffic. Added telemetry to monitor reauth count per-session.
notes_for_ops: When publishing pre-releases tag sdk-beta, route canary customer traffic with label 'sdk-beta' through the canary routing policy. Watch metric sdk.session.reauth_count and sdk.stream.reconnect_rate for 72 hours. If reauth_count spikes >2x baseline, rollback the client by unpublishing the pre-release and notify SDK owners.
merge_outcome: Merged to main after approvals from all reviewers and green CI. Pre-release artifacts published to internal registry.
